raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

`/v1/responses` omits `completed_at` even when `status` is `completed`, so OpenAI SDK clients always read `None`. Set the field from `ResponsesResponse.from_request`. Fixes #63183.

This does not duplicate an open PR.
[PR #63234](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63234) attempted the
same fix and was closed without merge.

AI assistance was used. The human submitter reviewed and understood every
changed line.

## Claims

- A completed Responses object includes `completed_at` as Unix seconds, and that value is greater than or equal to `created_at`.
- `queued`, `in_progress`, `incomplete`, `failed`, and `cancelled` responses include `completed_at: null`.
- Non-streaming responses, the final streaming event, and a stored background response all go through `from_request`, so they pick up the same field.

## Validation

Before the fix, on `main`'s `protocol.py`:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_serving_responses.py \
  -q -p no:cacheprovider -k test_completed_at_only_set_when_completed
```

6 failed. Each failure is `assert 'completed_at' in response`.

After the fix, the same command: 6 passed.

`tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_basic.py` asserts the field on the real OpenAI client for both unary and streaming responses. That test needs a model server and was not run on this CPU-only machine. CI's `entrypoints/openai/responses` step already collects that file.

All pre-commit hooks applicable to the four changed files passed, including
ruff, markdownlint, test tethering, mypy, and SPDX checks.

Spec: OpenAPI `components/schemas/Response.completed_at` (openai-openapi `master`, 2026-10-24) is a unixtime or null, "only present when the status is `completed`". `openai==2.44.0` `Response.completed_at` is `Optional[float]`.

## Details

Root cause: `ResponsesResponse` never declared `completed_at`, so response
serialization could not emit it. `from_request` is the shared constructor used
by the final object, the in-progress streaming snapshot, and the background
store update.

`completed_at` uses `int(time.time())` at construction, matching `created_at`. It is not copied from `created_at`, because generation can finish later. Cancelling a queued response only mutates `status`; that object was built with a non-completed status, so `completed_at` stays null.

No new sampling behavior and no benchmark.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

@@ -197,6 +197,9 @@ The following extra parameters are supported:
 Our Responses API is compatible with [OpenAI's Responses API](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/responses);
 you can use the [official OpenAI Python client](https://github.com/openai/openai-python) to interact with it.
 
+A response with `status` `completed` includes `completed_at`, the Unix time in
+seconds when generation finished. Every other status leaves `completed_at` null.
+
 Code example: [examples/tool_calling/openai_responses_client_with_tools.py](../../../examples/tool_calling/openai_responses_client_with_tools.py)
 
 To get prompt token IDs before generation, use

@@ -63,6 +63,8 @@ async def test_chat_with_input_type(client: openai.AsyncOpenAI):
     )
     print(response)
     assert response.status == "completed"
+    assert response.completed_at is not None
+    assert response.completed_at >= response.created_at
 
 
 @pytest.mark.asyncio
@@ -91,3 +93,6 @@ async def test_streaming(client: openai.AsyncOpenAI):
         for event in events
     )
     assert isinstance(events[-1], openai_responses_types.ResponseCompletedEvent)
+    assert events[0].response.completed_at is None
+    assert events[-1].response.completed_at is not None
+    assert events[-1].response.completed_at >= events[-1].response.created_at

@@ -2,6 +2,7 @@
 # SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
 
 import asyncio
+import time
 from collections import deque
 from contextlib import AsyncExitStack, asynccontextmanager
 from types import SimpleNamespace
@@ -223,6 +224,32 @@ def test_safety_identifier_defaults_to_none() -> None:
     assert _echoed_response()["safety_identifier"] is None
 
 
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "status",
+    ["completed", "queued", "in_progress", "incomplete", "failed", "cancelled"],
+)
+def test_completed_at_only_set_when_completed(status: str) -> None:
+    """OpenAI sets completed_at only for a completed Response."""
+    request = ResponsesRequest(model="test-model", input="hi")
+    before = int(time.time())
+    response = ResponsesResponse.from_request(
+        request=request,
+        sampling_params=request.to_sampling_params(default_max_tokens=16),
+        model_name="test-model",
+        created_time=before,
+        output=[],
+        status=status,
+    ).model_dump(mode="json")
+    after = int(time.time())
+
+    assert "completed_at" in response
+    if status == "completed":
+        assert before <= response["completed_at"] <= after
+        assert response["completed_at"] >= response["created_at"]
+    else:
+        assert response["completed_at"] is None
+
+
 @pytest.mark.parametrize(

+    completed_at: int | None = None
     # error: Optional[ResponseError] = None
     incomplete_details: IncompleteDetails | None = None
     instructions: str | None = None
@@ -980,6 +981,7 @@ def from_request(
